title: Evaluating Third-Party Audit Feasibility: What Can External Evaluators Actually Observe?

original_idea.body:
# Evaluating Third-Party Audit Feasibility: What Can External Evaluators Actually Observe?

**Problem:** Third-party adversarial evaluation of AI safety infrastructure is nascent. A key prerequisite question is: what can external evaluators actually observe without internal access, and is that sufficient for meaningful evaluation?

**Direction:** Define three access tiers for evaluating an agent monitoring system: black-box (API access only), gray-box (logs but no model weights), white-box (full access). Attempt monitoring evaluation under each tier. Measure what claims about monitoring quality can be supported under each access level.

**Why it matters:** Most third-party evaluators will have limited access. Understanding what claims are supportable at each access tier determines what third-party evaluations are actually worth.

**Relevant context:** METR 2026 third-party evaluation (white-box access); third-party audit feasibility; Anthropic collaboration model.
